review.verdict: The basic "jobs cut vs. power approved" gag reads, but half the brief's metaphor (the office cross-section, the second official racing a door that swings shut) never made it into the frame, and the palette/layout is too close to several recent blueprint-blue-and-yellow pieces to feel fresh.
revisionNotes: Add the office cross-section with rows of empty desks behind the worker/robot (institution cast element from the brief) so the robot visibly 'moves into' a vacated desk rather than standing on open ground.
Add the second official reaching a door that swings shut, briefcase mid-air, right of the datacenter — this is the whole 'ahead of a stricter governor' punchline and it's currently missing entirely.

Attach the box prop to the worker's hands/arms instead of floating detached above the head at the top anchor; same for the permit over the official — have the official actually hold/stamp it at chest height, scale 1.2, so it reads as an action not a wall decal.
Add the blueprint grid/graph-paper texture to the background; right now it's flat solid color and doesn't match the 'blueprint' style card the way other recent pieces do.

Swap the palette or composition pattern (navy background, yellow accents, robot flanked by two humans) — at least three recent sloppers use this same look, so novelty is weak; try a different accent color or vertical split instead of a flat ground line.
Use the empty bottom third: lower the horizon or add a small environmental detail (cable, power line, shadow) so the composition doesn't feel bottom-heavy with dead space.

review.verdict: The core gag reads clearly (sad worker replaced by a cheery robot vs. a happy official rubber-stamping the gas plant), but the second-official/door beat is badly clipped off the right edge, several props overlap messily, and the split-building blueprint composition repeats recent sloppers too closely — average score falls under the 3.5 pass bar.
revisionNotes: Second-official and door are clipped at the right canvas edge (lint confirms x up to 1071, well outside safe area) — move second-official to roughly x:0.82, scale 0.5, and reduce door's attach offset so the full hinged-door shape is visible inside the safe margin.
The door prop currently renders as a narrow sliver at the frame border — rebuild it at a smaller scale fully on-canvas so 'swinging shut, briefcase mid-air' actually reads as a beat, not noise.
Steam puffs from the datacenter overlap the permit's checkmark corner — shift permit offset up-left by ~20px or move steam puffs behind the datacenter stack so the checkmark stays clean.

The moving box attached to worker reads as a vague pale wedge melting into the robot's leg — bump its scale to ~1.0 and nudge it fully in front of the worker's body so it reads unambiguously as a carried box.

Composition leans on the same left/right split-building-vs-robot blueprint layout as recent frames (e.g. the resigned/your-problem and chief-resigns/rival-launches sloppers) — vary the horizon break or swap one side to a non-building silhouette for more novelty.
Power-line prop bleeds past the bottom safe margin per the lint warning; shorten its width or raise y slightly so the poles don't clip the edge.

review.verdict: The left half (worker out, robot in) reads instantly, but the right half is let down by a face/permit overlap bug, an uneven scale between tiny smokestack/datacenter and full-size figures, a missing brief element (the second official racing the door), and a composition that closely echoes a recent blueprint split-scene piece — it falls short of publish quality.
revisionNotes: Fix the overlap bug: the permit panel (at x0.64,y0.44) clips directly over the official's face (head at x0.58,y0.74) leaving a stray dark fragment visible — reposition the permit to the official's right side via attachTo/offset so the face stays clear.

The brief's second beat — 'a second official reaching a door just as it swings shut, briefcase mid-air' — is missing entirely from the scene; add it so the 'ahead of a stricter governor taking office' urgency actually reads.

Scale up datacenter (currently 0.65) and smokestack (90x360, very thin) to match the visual weight of the office building on the left; the right half currently reads as a cluster of small afterthoughts next to two full-size figures.
Pull the smokestack in from x=0.9 so it isn't crowding the right edge of the safe area.

This is the fourth blueprint-palette, two-top-label split-scene composition in the recent batch (near-identical to the 'Resigned / Your Problem' piece) — vary the background type or label placement for novelty.
Give the official an active stamping pose rather than a static permit-hold to sell 'approved' as an action, reinforcing the race-against-time beat from the brief.
